
  The rise of graphical user interfaces in the 1990s pushed terminals out of
  sight, but developers never stopped using them. SSH encrypted remote access,
  Putty carried terminals across Windows networks, and today web-based shells
  let anyone run Linux commands from a browser. Terminals remain fundamental:
  they are still how systems administrators manage servers, how developers
  deploy code, and how curious people explore computing beyond what icons
  provide.

  Light clicks keys, A screen fills with ghosts of letters, Time flows in
  silence.
